questions.stem: Which of the following checks to see if the assessable record exists for the demand and creates an assessable record if none exists?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Demand > Assessments: The Auto Business Rule for Assessments (B) checks whether an assessable record exists for a demand and creates one if none exists. This BR automatically handles the assessable record lifecycle for demand assessment metrics. Validate Assessment Metrics (A) evaluates metrics, Update Demand State (C) handles workflow, and Create OnDemand Assessment (D) is a different trigger mechanism.

questions.stem: Projects and which other artifact can be linked to either a program, a portfolio, both, or neither.
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Portfolio > Linked Artifacts: Projects and Demands (A) can both be linked to a program, a portfolio, both, or neither. They are the primary planning artifacts in Portfolio Management. Test Cases (B) are QA artifacts. Resources (C) and Stories (D) are not standalone artifacts at the portfolio/program hierarchy level.

questions.stem: If Scenario Planning for PPM is installed, a portfolio manager can access the Portfolio Planning Workbench by navigating to which of the following? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Portfolio Planning Workbench > Access: Two access points for the Portfolio Planning Workbench are: the Portfolio Planning related link (C) on the Portfolio form, and the Portfolio Planning Workbench module (D) in the application navigator under Project > Portfolios. (p1534) Project module (A) and Program Workbench (B) do not provide direct access to the Portfolio Planning Workbench.

questions.stem: When creating a resource plan within a demand, how are the default dates on a resource plan determined?

options.text: From demand start date and due date
Resource plan(s) cannot be created from demand

questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Resource Plans > Default Dates: When creating a resource plan within a demand, the default dates are derived from the demand's start date and due date (A). This ensures the resource plan aligns with the demand's scheduled timeline. Resource plans CAN be created from a demand (B is false). Using created date (C) or portfolio date (D) would not reflect the demand schedule.

questions.stem: A customer requires five (5) teamspaces to support different departments. What should you do?

options.text: Contact the Account Representative to activate the teamspaces.
Use UI Policies and Business Rules to enable teamspaces.

questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Teamspaces > Activation: To support 5 teamspaces, activate via each teamspace plugin (C). ServiceNow provides separate plugins for each teamspace: com.snc.ppm_teamspace_1 through com.snc.ppm_teamspace_5 (p1137). Each plugin must be activated individually. There is no single teamspace property (A). Account Reps handle licensing (B), not technical activation. UI Policies/BRs (D) are not involved.

questions.stem: When setting-up a program, planned ROI% is calculated based on: (Choose two.)

options.text: Values in the Planned cost field.
Values in the Planned return field.
Values in the Budgeted cost field.

questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Programs > Planned ROI: Planned ROI% is calculated from values in the Planned return field (C) and the Planned cost field (B). The formula per p1541 is: Planned return / Planned cost × 100. NPV (A) is calculated separately as present value of future cash. Budgeted cost (D) is an actual budget figure, not used in the ROI% formula.

questions.stem: Which plugin provides a layer of artificial intelligence that empowers features and capabilities across applications to provide better work experiences?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > AI > Predictive Intelligence: Predictive Intelligence for PPM [com.snc.ppm_ml] (C) provides the AI/ML layer that empowers features across PPM applications. It supports similar demand detection, duplicate avoidance, and project prediction. (p945) Strategic Spend Tracking (A) handles budget governance. Scenario Planning (B) manages portfolio scenarios. PPM Standard (D) is the base financial/project plugin.

questions.stem: To use the Time Sheet dashboard, what plugin must be installed?

options.text: Common ITSM Service Portal Application Components (com.snc.app_common.service_portal)
Performance Analytics – Content Pack – PPM Standard plugin (com.snc.pa.pmo_dashboards)

questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Dashboards > Time Sheet: The Performance Analytics - Content Pack - PPM Standard plugin [com.snc.pa.pmo_dashboards] (D) must be installed to use the Time Sheet dashboard. This plugin provides PA content packs including dashboards for PPM workstreams. The other plugins (A, B, C) are ITSM, HR, and Knowledge Management plugins unrelated to PPM dashboards.

questions.stem: Where do you define ‘Roles’ requested via resource plans?

options.text: No need to define it differently, they are same are system roles

questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Resource Management > Roles: Resource roles requested via resource plans are defined under Resource roles in the Resource Management application (A). Resource roles (such as Developer, Architect) are distinct from system security roles and are managed separately. They are not the same as system roles (B). Skill Management (C) handles competencies. System Security (D) roles control platform access.

questions.stem: Plugins may be added to the base platform in one of the following ways: (Choose three.)

options.text: Activated by an admin (not by default).
Activated by default in the base ServiceNow system.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Plugins > Activation Methods: Three ways plugins can be added are: activated by an admin (not by default) (A) for optional plugins, requested from ServiceNow (C) for specialized plugins requiring ServiceNow involvement, and activated by default in the base system (D) for standard included plugins. it_portfolio_manager (B) and it_pps_admin (E) are functional roles without system plugin activation rights.

questions.stem: What does the project status report allow project managers to do? (Choose two.)

options.text: Show historical trend of project KPI’s

questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Project > Status Reports: Project status reports allow project managers to: show historical trend of project KPIs (C) — reports capture snapshots over time — and print as a PDF attachment (D). (p1360 confirms print capability). Gantt chart viewing (A) is in the project workspace, not status reports. WBS viewing (B) is a separate project tool, not specific to status reports.

questions.stem: How does a project manager request a change to a resource plan in the requested state?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Resource Plans > Change Request: A project manager requests a change to a resource plan in the Requested state by using the Request Change action on the resource plan (C). This creates a formal change request that the resource manager reviews. Notes (A) are informational only. Emailing the resource user (B) or resource manager (D) are informal channels, not the platform's built-in mechanism.

questions.stem: In which table can you find cost information for a specific fiscal period?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Cost Plans > Fiscal Period Data: Cost information for a specific fiscal period is found in the cost_plan_breakdown table (C). Per p949, Cost Plan Breakdown [cost_plan_breakdown] specifies estimated and actual costs at a granular level for a fiscal period. cost_plan (A) holds the overall plan. expense_line (B) tracks expenses. pm_project (D) is the project record.

questions.stem: What is the default schedule for a project?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Projects > Default Schedule: The default project schedule is an 8-hour workday from 8 to 12 and 1 to 5 (A). Per p1126, the default is 'Monday to Friday workday from 8 A.M. to 5 P.M. with an hour break for lunch.' This is 4 hours morning + 4 hours afternoon = 8 hours/day. Options B (9-12 and 1-6) and D (9-5 straight) don't match the documented default.

questions.stem: The PPM Standard plugin enables an it_project_manager to perform the following activities: (Choose three.)

options.text: Establish resource requirements and track costs.
Track actual amount spent compared to an approved budget.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > it_project_manager > Capabilities: Three activities enabled by PPM Standard for a project manager are: determine overall project cost requirements (A), establish resource requirements and track costs (D), and track actual amount spent vs approved budget (E). Configuring cost type definitions (B) is an admin configuration task. Defining portfolio targets (C) is the portfolio manager's function.

questions.stem: When a time card is approved, the actual time is stored in which two tables? (Choose two.)

options.text: Resource Aggregate tables (Daily, Weekly, and Monthly)

questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Time Cards > Storage: When a time card is approved, actual time is stored in the Resource Allocation Daily table (B) and the Resource Aggregate tables (D). Per p1812, Resource Allocation Daily [resource_allocation_daily] stores actual hours, and Resource Aggregate Daily [resource_aggregate_daily] stores aggregated capacity/allocated/confirmed hours. Project Time (A) and Resource Event (C) are not the correct tables.

questions.stem: Which of the following roles can access the project administration application?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Roles > Project Administration: The it_pps_admin role (B) can access the project administration application. Per p1815, the PPS Admin role has broad administrative access including project diagnostics and system configuration. it_project_user (A) has view-only access. it_project_manager (C) has project configuration access. timecard_admin (D) manages time cards only.

questions.stem: The Project Portfolio Management application supports domain separation at this level:
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Domain Separation > Level: PPM supports domain separation at Level 1 - Tenant data management (B). Per p187, 'The application supports domain separation at the Basic level' with data separation as the support model. Basic/Level 1 means data goes into the proper domain but business logic is not fully domain-separated. Level 2 (C) process management and Level 3 (A) are not supported.

questions.stem: The hourly rate is derived from the resource rate on the resource plan, if this option is selected.
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Resource Plans > Hourly Rate: The hourly rate is derived from the resource rate on the resource plan when the Rate Override option is selected (A). Per p1473: 'Planned Cost = Planned hours × hourly rate. The hourly rate is derived from...Resource rate from the resource plan, if the Rate O[verride option is selected].' Labor rate card (B) and Rate model (C) are fallback sources. Planned cost (D) is the result.

questions.stem: Which role can configure the parameters of the demand workbench that is provided with the base system?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Demand Workbench > Configuration: The it_pps_admin role (C) can configure the parameters of the demand workbench. Per p960: 'Before you begin Role required: it_pps_admin.' The PPS Admin has full administrative access to workbench configuration including bubble chart parameters. All roles (A), it_project_manager (B), and business_stakeholder (D) do not have this configuration access.

questions.stem: Depending on the execution type selected for a particular project, one of these dashboards will also be available:
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Project Workspace > Execution-Type Dashboards: Depending on the execution type, the Project Summary - Waterfall Dashboard (C) becomes available in the Analytics tab of Project Workspace. Waterfall, Agile, and Hybrid execution types each surface a relevant dashboard. Timecard Dashboard (A) and User Manager Dashboard (B) are time management tools. PMO Dashboard (D) is a general overview, not execution-type specific.

questions.stem: In order to submit an idea, what application would a user access?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Ideation > Submission Access: Users submit ideas through the Idea Portal (C). Per p942, ideas can be submitted via Service Catalog > Submit Idea or Self-Service > Ideas > Create New — both routes use the Idea Portal interface. The Demand application (A) is for existing demands. Project (B) and Change (D) are different ITSM/PM artifacts.

questions.stem: Which ‘Member Preference’ automatically finds the most available resource(s) from the group and allocates to a plan using the allocation action?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Resource Plans > Member Preference: The 'Any member' preference (D) automatically finds the most available resource from the group and allocates to the plan. When 'Any member' is selected, the system evaluates all group members and picks the one with the most available capacity. 'All members' (A) distributes to everyone. 'Specific member' (B) requires manual selection.

questions.stem: An it_pps_admin user is able to update: (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > it_pps_admin > Update Capabilities: An it_pps_admin can update Budget Periods (A) and Portfolio Targets (D). Budget Periods are fiscal planning configurations managed by the PPS Admin. Portfolio Targets define CAPEX/OPEX goals per fiscal year. Client Scripts (B) and Business Rules (C) require system admin/developer roles, not pps_admin.

questions.stem: What role can configure an idea module, map idea categories to the idea module, and add navigation for the Idea Portal?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Idea Portal > Admin Role: The idea_admin role (A) can configure an idea module, map idea categories, and add navigation for the Idea Portal. Per p925: 'Role required: idea_admin' for creating idea modules. idea_manager (C) evaluates ideas but doesn't configure the module. it_project_manager (B) and it_demand_manager (D) are unrelated to idea module configuration.

questions.stem: Which roles can view reports on resource utilization and availability? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Resource Reports > View Roles: Two roles that can view reports on resource utilization and availability are resource_manager (C) and resource_user (D). Resource managers and users both have access to resource reports to monitor capacity, allocations, and availability. it_project_portfolio_user (A) views portfolio records. pps_resource (B) is a basic resource assignment role without reporting access.

questions.stem: What role can create or modify a rate model?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Rate Models > Management Role: The it_pps_admin role (A) can create or modify a rate model. Rate models are system-level configurations for cost calculation that fall under PPS Admin's administrative domain. time_card_admin (B) manages time tracking. push_admin (C) and release_admin (D) are not standard PPM roles.

questions.stem: To set up a group for selection in a resource plan, the group record needs to include which role?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Resource Groups > Required Role: The group record needs to include the pps_resource role (D) for the group to be selectable in a resource plan. Per p1436, users in the Resource Manager view are those with pps_resource role, and groups must have this role for resource planning. resource_manager (A) is the allocation manager. itil (B) and it_project_user (C) are unrelated to resource group selection.

questions.stem: When can a user choose from multiple rate types for their work, while logging a time card?

options.text: Only if the capability is enabled in the Project Preferences
Only if this capability is enabled in the Project Record
Only one (1) rate type can apply
Only if the capability is enabled in the Time Sheet Policies

questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Time Cards > Multiple Rate Types: A user can choose from multiple rate types while logging a time card only if the capability is enabled in the Time Sheet Policies (D). Per p1564, the 'Allow multiple rate types' option is a Time Sheet Policy configuration. This is not a project preference (A, B) setting. Only one rate type can apply per time card unless this policy option is enabled.

questions.stem: What is the difference between confirm and allocate actions?

options.text: Confirm action creates hard allocation and allocate action creates soft allocation.
Confirm action creates soft allocation and allocate action creates hard allocation.
Allocate action is always followed by confirm action.

questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Resource Plans > Confirm vs Allocate: Confirm creates a soft allocation and Allocate creates a hard allocation (C). Confirming a resource plan tentatively assigns the resource (soft booking), while the Allocate action commits the resource (hard booking) and creates calendar events. Per p1410, soft allocations are converted to hard allocations when the resource plan moves to Allocated state.

questions.stem: If a user creates a new demand from the demand workbench, what state will the system save the record in?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Demand Workbench > New Demand State: When a user creates a new demand from the demand workbench, the system saves the record in the Qualified state (D). Per p964: 'Demands created from the Demand Workbench are in the Qualified state.' This differs from demands created through other paths (like Create New), which start in Draft state.

questions.stem: In order for a business unit to have its own Idea Portal to retrieve data, what must be configured first?

options.text: A business unit cannot have its own its own Idea Portal

questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Idea Portal > Prerequisite: For a business unit to have its own Idea Portal, an Idea module (D) must be configured first. Each business unit uses a separate Idea Module, which defines the idea table and portal URL (via Module ID). Per p939, the Module Id is used in the Idea Portal URL. The Idea Portal URL (B) and Idea categories (C) are configured after the module.

questions.stem: What needs to be configured if a customer wants to change the attributes copied when using copy project or copy partial project?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Copy Project > Additional Attributes: To change the attributes copied during copy project or copy partial project, configure the com.snc.project.copy.additional_attributes system property (C). This property controls which additional fields are copied when a project is duplicated. The copy project UI action (D) handles execution but not attribute configuration. com.snc.project.copy (B) is less specific.

questions.stem: When entering time worked into a time sheet, which feature is recommended to group different types of work (e.g., standard hours and overtime)?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Time Sheets > Work Type Grouping: Rate type (A) is the recommended feature for grouping different types of work in a time sheet. Per p1566: 'Rate type functionality is used to categorize different types of work. For example, Standard versus Overtime.' Users select a rate type when logging time to distinguish work categories. Bill rate (B), Category (C), and Rate model (D) serve different purposes.

questions.stem: What system role is needed to manage programs?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Programs > Management Role: The system role needed to manage programs is it_program_manager (C). Per p1958, 'Program manager [it_program_manager] - Users with this role have full control on all scrum programs.' it_project_manager (A) manages projects specifically. it_portfolio_manager_admin (B) and it_program_manager_admin (D) are not standard ServiceNow PPM role names.

questions.stem: Who can submit Ideas?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Ideation > Submitters: Any user (A) can submit ideas. Per p942: 'Any user can submit ideas from Service Catalog > Submit Idea or Self-Service > Ideas > Create New.' Idea submission is not restricted to IT users (B), demand users (C), or ITIL users (D). This openness encourages innovation across the organization.

questions.stem: Where can a user export project data in either a MPP, XML or CSV format?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Project Export > Location: Project data can be exported in MPP, XML, or CSV format from the Planning Console (D). Per p1125-1126, the export module, project form, or Planning Console can be used to save project data in these formats. The Planning Console provides direct export access for project managers. Demand Form (A) and Related lists (B) don't support this export.

questions.stem: Which of the following are true regarding how the My Project Space (Project Workspace) handles dynamic content? (Choose two.)

options.text: If the project state is On Hold, actual start date and actual end date are displayed.
If the project state is Pending or Open, planned start date and planned end date are displayed.
If the project state is Draft, actual start date and actual end date are displayed.
If the project state is Work in Progress, actual start date and planned end date are displayed.

questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Project Workspace > Dynamic Dates: Two true statements about dynamic date display are: Pending or Open state shows planned start and planned end dates (B) and Work in Progress state shows actual start and planned end dates (D). Per p1051: 'Pending/Open: Planned start date is displayed' and 'Work in Progress: Actual start date is displayed' with planned end date for ongoing projects.

questions.stem: Which of the following states appear in the process flow indicator at the top of the Demand form by default? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Demand Form > Process Flow States: Three states shown in the process flow indicator by default are: Draft (A), Approved (B), and Screening (D). These represent the main linear progression of a demand: Draft → Screening → Approved. Updated (C) is an action/button, not a state. Deferred (E) is a branch-off state not shown in the main process flow.

questions.stem: Where are CAPEX and OPEX targets set for each fiscal year?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Portfolio > CAPEX/OPEX Targets: CAPEX and OPEX targets are set for each fiscal year in the Portfolio Target (C). Per p1482: 'Enter the CAPEX and OPEX target for each fiscal year. This target amount is split equally among the fiscal periods. The portfolio target is included in the Portfolio Target related list.' Demand Workbench (A), Cost Plans (B), and Program Workbench (D) do not set these targets.

questions.stem: Which plugin activates the ideas module to gather and evaluate ideas efficiently, and quickly identify ideas for implementation?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Ideation > Plugin: The Ideation with PPM [com.snc.ppm_innovation_management] plugin (C) activates the ideas module to gather, evaluate, and identify ideas for implementation. Per p1806, it 'enables your organization to collect new ideas, collaborate on ideas, and identify great ideas for implementation.' Resource Management (A), Test Management (B), and Agile Development (D) serve different purposes.

questions.stem: In what way would you restrict the assigned to field on a project task to only allow users with resource allocations to be assigned?

options.text: Create an Access Control List (ACL) rule.
On the project record under the preferences tab select the “Derive assignee list from resource plan” preference.
The system automatically does this and can only be disabled by an admin.
Create a reference qualifier on the ‘assigned to’ field.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Project Tasks > Assignee Restriction: To restrict the assigned to field to only users with resource allocations, select the 'Derive assignee list from resource plan' preference on the project record's Preferences tab (B). This project-level preference filters the assignee list based on resource plans. ACLs (A) and reference qualifiers (D) would be workarounds, not the intended configuration.

questions.stem: At a minimum, which role is required to view the summary of a project in the Details tab of Project Workspace?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Project Workspace > Minimum Role: The minimum role required to view the summary in the Details tab of Project Workspace is it_project_user (C). Per p1350: 'Before you begin Role required: it_project_user.' it_project_manager (A) and it_portfolio_manager (D) have higher access levels. The itil role (B) is an ITSM role with no PPM access.

questions.stem: What is the demand workbench used for? (Choose two.)

options.text: Comparing and prioritizing demands against other demands.

questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Demand Workbench > Purpose: Two uses of the demand workbench are: displaying submitted demands to stakeholders (A) and comparing and prioritizing demands against other demands (C). Per p963, it 'provides a single point of engagement for assessing demands' combining an interactive bubble chart with a demands list. While approval is possible, comparing/displaying demands are its primary functions.

questions.stem: What applications are shared across teamspaces?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Teamspaces > Shared Applications: Resource, Agile, and Test applications (C) are shared across teamspaces. These cross-functional applications serve all teamspaces rather than being duplicated per teamspace. Project Financials (in options A, B) is teamspace-specific. Only Resource, Agile, and Test are the three applications shared across all teamspaces.

questions.stem: A project expense line is a cost associated with a specific source. Examples of specific sources could include: (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Expense Lines > Sources: Three examples of specific sources for a project expense line are: User (A), Configuration Item/CI (B), and Fixed Asset (E). Per p977, 'a demand expense line is the cost associated with a specific source, such as a user or a fixed asset.' CIs are also valid sources. Project (C) is the container for the expense, not a specific source. Demand (D) is not listed as a source type.

questions.stem: Which roles can modify agile properties? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Agile > Property Modification Roles: Two roles that can modify agile properties are it_pps_admin (A) and admin (C). The PPS Admin has broad PPM administrative access and the system admin has full platform access. product_owner (B) and scrum_master (D) are functional agile roles without system property configuration rights.

questions.stem: In the base system, what is the default number of cards that can be displayed in the project workspace?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Project Workspace > Card Limit: The default maximum number of cards displayed in project workspace is 200 (A). Per p1340: 'A maximum of the 200 most recently updated projects appear on the page.' The cards are ordered by most recently updated. The values 10 (B), 1500 (C), and 1 (D) are incorrect.

questions.stem: Demand managers can enhance a demand request by adding the following: (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Demand Management > Enhancements: Three items demand managers can add to enhance a demand are: Requirements (A), Decisions (D), and Stakeholders (E). Per p988, demand managers can add requirements, and the docs confirm decisions and stakeholders are demand-related artifacts. Change Requests (B) and Problems (C) are ITSM artifacts, not standard demand enhancement items.

questions.stem: This should be updated by an it_pps_admin, so that the stakeholder list will automatically populate when a user creates a demand or project.
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Stakeholder Registry > Auto-populate: The Stakeholder Registry (B) should be updated by an it_pps_admin so that the stakeholder list automatically populates when creating a demand or project. Per p1036, the Stakeholder Register Form adds users to the Stakeholder Registry, which then drives the auto-population of stakeholder lists on demand and project forms.

questions.stem: What happens to the expense line after it is processed?

options.text: The actual cost is recorded at the portfolio level.
The actual amount incurred becomes part of the cost plan.

questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Expense Lines > Processing Result: After an expense line is processed, the actual amount incurred becomes part of the cost plan (D). Per p1077: 'Once the expense line is processed, the actual amount incurred becomes part of the cost plan.' The actual amount spent is recorded against the cost plan, contributing to total actual costs. It does not close the cost plan (C) or record only at portfolio level (A).

questions.stem: A pps_admin role can configure the parameters that are displayed on a project card. The parameters displayed on a project card are derived from the records in what table?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Project Workspace > Card Configuration: The parameters on a project card are derived from records in the PM Home Page Card [pm_home_page_card] table (B). Per p1344, card configuration is managed in the PM Home Page Configuration [pm_home_page_config] table, with the card parameters stored in pm_home_page_card. CMDB Scorecard (A), Time Card Exception (C), and Scrum Theme (D) are unrelated tables.

questions.stem: What creates calendar entries on a user’s individual calendar? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Resource Plans > Calendar Entries: Confirmed (C) and Planned (D) resource plans create calendar entries on a user's individual calendar. When resource plans are in these states, the system automatically generates calendar events within the user's work schedule. Approved (A) is not a standard resource plan state. Allocated (B) plans also affect calendars but are not the two that create the initial calendar entries.

questions.stem: If the Agile Development 2.0 plugin is activated, an idea can be converted into which of the following task types? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Ideation > Agile Conversions: With Agile Development 2.0 activated, an idea can be converted into: Story (A), Epic (C), and Project (E). Per p922, the task options with Agile 2.0 include Demand, Project, Epic, and Story. SAFe epic (B) and SAFe feature (D) require the separate Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe) plugin, not just Agile 2.0.

questions.stem: The RIDAC workflow can be modified by using which feature?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > RIDAC > Workflow Modification: The RIDAC (Risks, Issues, Decisions, Actions, Changes) workflow can be modified using Flow Designer (D). Flow Designer is the modern tool for customizing workflows and automated processes in ServiceNow. The Project Form (A), Service Catalog (B), and Idea Portal (C) do not provide RIDAC workflow modification capabilities.

questions.stem: An it_project_manager can request resources by which of the following: (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Resource Plans > Request Types: A project manager can request resources by Hours (A) and Person Days (B). These are the two resource request types available: specifying hours directly, or using person days. FTE is another option in some contexts. Month (C) and Day (D) are time durations, not resource request unit types in ServiceNow PPM.

questions.stem: Which of these tools allow you pinpoint over-allocated resources by viewing their negative availability values? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Resource Management > Over-allocation Tools: Two tools that show over-allocated resources via negative availability values are: Resource Allocation Workbench (C) and Resource Reports (D). The Resource Allocation Workbench displays availability across resources and highlights negative values indicating over-allocation. Resource Reports provide similar visibility. Project Workbench (A) focuses on tasks. Resource Plan Logs (B) tracks plan changes.

questions.stem: How is a resource group’s capacity derived for resource planning?

options.text: Aggregate capacity of all its members.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Resource Groups > Capacity: A resource group's capacity is derived from the aggregate capacity of all its members (A). The group capacity = sum of individual member capacities based on their schedules and availability. This is the derivation method. Resource_Aggregate_Daily (B) stores the computed values but doesn't explain how capacity is derived. The group record (C) does not store capacity.

questions.stem: The information displayed on Project Workspace is setup in which table?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Project Workspace > Display Table: The information displayed on Project Workspace is set up in the pm_home_page_card table (C). Per p1344, card configuration (rows 2 and 3) is managed in the PM Home Page Configuration [pm_home_page_config] table, derived from pm_home_page_card records. vtb_card (A) is Visual Task Board. pm_project (B) is the project data table. vtb_card_history (D) is VTB history.

questions.stem: Which capability allows users to view variances in a project’s schedule?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Projects > Schedule Variance: The Compare scheduled baselines capability (C) allows users to view variances in a project's schedule. Per p1276, comparing baselines 'helps you understand the real-time deviations between planned and actual values.' Move project (A) reschedules tasks. Status Reports (B) show current state snapshots. Machine-learning (D) is for finding similar projects.

questions.stem: What role can configure the default columns in the project planning console? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Planning Console > Column Configuration Roles: Two roles that can configure default columns in the project planning console are admin (A) and it_pps_admin (D). Per p1174, planning console display columns are configured under Project Administration settings. The it_pps_admin role manages all project administration settings, and admin has full system access. it_project_manager (B) and it_console_admin (C) do not have project administration settings access.

questions.stem: Which table stores daily capacity of a user?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Resource Tables > Daily Capacity Storage: The Resource Aggregate Daily table (A) stores daily capacity of a user. Per p1812: 'Resource Aggregate Daily [resource_aggregate_daily] - On a day-to-day basis, stores aggregated values, such as capacity, allocated hours in a project, confirmed hours.' Resource Allocation Daily (B) stores resource plan events and actual hours, not capacity. User Profile (C) and Resource Event (D) do not store daily aggregated capacity.

questions.stem: Users with what role can be considered for resource planning?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Resource Management > Planning Role: Users with the pps_resource role (B) can be considered for resource planning. Per p1436: 'Resource Manager view lists only the users who have the pps_resource role.' Per p1817: 'PPS resource [pps_resource] - Only users with this role' appear as allocatable resources. it_user (A), it_project_user (C), and it_pps_user (D) are not the role that makes users available for resource planning.

questions.stem: What features are not included in a teamspace application but can be added in teamspace settings? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Teamspaces > Optional Settings: Two features not included in a teamspace application by default but can be added in teamspace settings are Workbench configuration (A) and Demand Assessments (D). Teamspace plugins include Project and Demand tables by default. Workbench configuration and Demand Assessment features can be enabled via teamspace administration settings. Idea (B) requires the separate Ideation plugin. Project (C) is included by default in every teamspace.

questions.stem: Is resource capacity derived from FTE or schedules?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Resource Management > Capacity Derivation: Resource capacity is derived only from Schedules (C), not from FTE. Per p1402: 'Capacity is not derived from FTE, but from schedules. Both FTE and schedules must be in synchronization with each other.' FTE is used to calculate planned hours, but capacity itself is schedule-driven. Options A (Only FTE) and B (Both) are incorrect per this explicit doc statement.

questions.stem: How is the Resource Management application activated?

options.text: Installed as part of Release Management plugin
Installed as part of adding users
Installed automatically as part of new system

questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Resource Management > Activation: The Resource Management application is installed with the PPM Standard plugin (A). Per p910: 'Activate the PPM Standard plugin (com.snc.financial_planning_pmo)... This plugin installs the Project Portfolio Management applications.' Resource Management is one of the core PPM applications included in this plugin. It is not part of Release Management (B), user setup (C), or automatic system installation (D).

questions.stem: Can an it_project_manager convert a task to a milestone?

options.text: Yes, it must be manually done from the project record.
Yes, from the planning console right-click a task and select convert to milestone.
No, the task must be deleted and re-created.
No, this can only be done by an admin.

questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Planning Console > Task to Milestone: An it_project_manager can convert a task to a milestone by right-clicking on the task in the Planning Console (B). Per p1086: 'You can also convert a task to milestone through Planning console tasks.' This sets Duration to 0, creating a diamond milestone symbol. Manual project form editing (A) is not the method. PPS admin (C) or system admin (D) roles are not required for this action.

questions.stem: Which field on the Idea Module form displays the unique identifier for the module, that is used as a parameter in the Idea Portal URL to direct users?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Idea Module > URL Identifier Field: The Module ID field (A) displays the unique identifier used as a parameter in the Idea Portal URL. Per p939: 'Module Id - Unique identifier for the module used as a parameter in the Idea Portal URL to direct users. For example, if you use hr as the Module Id, the URL would look like: /idea/?id=ideas_list&sysparm_module_id=hr.' Category Limit (B), Module Name (C), and Idea Table (D) serve different purposes.

questions.stem: Which users have access the project administration application? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Project Administration > Access Roles: Two roles with access to the project administration application are it_pps_admin (B) and admin (D). Per p1815, it_pps_admin 'Can view and modify project administration settings' — this is the primary PPM admin role. Admin has full system-level access including project administration. it_portfolio_manager (A) manages portfolios but not project administration settings. it_project_manager (C) manages projects, not admin settings.

questions.stem: The Business Unit field on a Project or displays values from a specific table. What type of field is this?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Project Form > Business Unit Field Type: The Business Unit field on a Project form is a Reference field (A). It stores a reference to a record in the Business Unit table, allowing the field to display values from that specific table. This is the standard ServiceNow field type for cross-table lookups. Conditions (B), Journal (C), and List (D) are different field types not used for business unit lookups.

questions.stem: If an it_project_manager does not want to equally distribute hours across the resource plan time frame, what allocation spread should be used?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Resource Plans > Unequal Allocation Spread: If an it_project_manager does not want to equally distribute hours, Front Load (A) allocation spread should be used. Front Load concentrates allocated hours toward the beginning of the resource plan period, unlike Even (D) which splits hours uniformly across all working days. Back Load (B) concentrates hours at the end. The allocation spread selection is configured on the resource plan form.

questions.stem: Using the Request type field on a resource plan, which options can be used to request a resource? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Resource Plans > Request Type Options: Three options for the Request type field on a resource plan are Hours (B), FTE (C), and Person Days (D). Per p1467, the Request type field determines how requested allocation is measured: by specific hours, FTE units, or person-day equivalents. Month (A) and Day (E) are not valid request type options in the Resource Plan form.

questions.stem: What are the possible breakdown types of a cost plan breakdown? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Cost Plans > Breakdown Types: Four possible breakdown types for a cost plan breakdown are Demand (A), Project (C), Portfolio (E), and Program (F). Per p1053: 'If a project or demand is part of a program, the breakdown type of Program provides aggregate costs. If part of a portfolio, the breakdown type of Portfolio provides aggregate costs.' Demand and Project are the base container types. Requirement (B) and Task (D) are not cost plan breakdown types.

questions.stem: Where is planned cost calculated from when requesting resources from a group and when resource role is specified?

options.text: The hourly rate of the specified role.

questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Resource Plans > Planned Cost Calculation: When requesting resources from a group with a resource role specified, planned cost is calculated from the hourly rate of the specified role (C). Per p1461: 'While requesting resources from a group, if a resource role is specified, the planned cost is calculated from the hourly rate of the specified role.' Task rate cards (A), distribution costs (B), and CI rate cards (D) are not used in this calculation scenario.

questions.stem: What is a Program?

options.text: A group of related projects and program activities.
A group of related projects, ideas, demands, and task activities.
A group of related projects, demands, and program activities.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Programs > Definition: A Program is a group of related projects, demands, and program activities (C). Per p1536: 'A program helps you to logically group related projects or demands under a single entity.' Per p1542, programs contain Projects, Demands, and Program Tasks (activities). Option A omits demands. Option B adds ideas (which are a separate Innovation Management concept). Option D is too narrow — programs also include demands.

questions.stem: If you want the project planned start date to remain the same despite the start date of the earliest task, what property would you disable?

options.text: Roll up project start date from tasks [com.snc.project.rollup_project_start_date].
Max date span into future or past from the current date for the project/project task [com.snc.project.task.check_date_span_years].
Retain start on constraint on tasks after adding relations [com.snc.project.allow_start_on_relations].
Max duration allowed for a project/project task [com.snc.project.task.max_task_duration].

questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Project Properties > Start Date Rollup: To keep the project planned start date unchanged despite the earliest task start date, disable the Roll up project start date from tasks property (A) — com.snc.project.rollup_project_start_date. When enabled, this property pushes the earliest task start date to the project level. Disabling it fixes the project start date independently of tasks. Options B, C, and D control date span, task constraints, and duration limits respectively.

questions.stem: Which is the minimum role that has access to the Project Administration > Settings > Preferences-Project module?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Project Admin Settings > Preferences Role: The minimum role to access Project Administration > Settings > Preferences-Project is it_pps_admin (B). Per p1815, it_pps_admin 'Can view and modify project administration settings,' which includes preferences. sys_admin (C) has access but is not the minimum PPM-specific role. it_project_manager (A) manages projects but lacks project administration settings access. it_program_manager (D) is scoped to programs.

questions.stem: When creating a project from demand, what related records are moved and copied upon Project Creation?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Demand to Project > Moved Records: When creating a project from a demand, the Resource Plan and Cost Plan (A) are moved and copied upon project creation. Resource plans are transferred to the new project to maintain continuity of resource allocations. Cost plans carry over the financial planning data. Change Requests (B) are RIDAC elements. Assessments (C) are demand-specific evaluation records. The Idea and Demand (D) remain as linked records, not moved.

questions.stem: How many WBS levels can be shown on the planning console?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Planning Console > WBS Levels: There is no limit (D) to the number of WBS levels that can be shown on the planning console. The planning console supports unlimited nesting of tasks in the work breakdown structure hierarchy. This allows project managers to create deeply nested project structures as needed without hitting a system limit. Options A, B, and C incorrectly suggest specific caps on WBS nesting.

questions.stem: What is a data copy of the current project’s task, schedule, or structure that can be used for comparison reporting later?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Baselines > Definition: A Baseline (D) is a data copy of the current project's tasks, schedule, or structure used for comparison reporting. Per p1276: 'A baseline is a snapshot of the project's progress at the particular moment of time.' Baselines enable schedule and financial variance analysis by comparing current vs. baseline values. Accrual (A) tracks recognized costs. Forecast (B) is a future projection. Commitment (C) refers to allocated/confirmed resources.

questions.stem: A checklist item record provides a name and what other element?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Checklists > Record Fields: A checklist item record provides only a name and a Complete field (B), which can be set to true or false. Per p1051: 'a checklist item record provides only a name and a Complete field, which can be set to true or false.' Checklist items do not have Status (A), Percent complete (C), or Short description (D) fields.

questions.stem: The project property to update actual effort from time card is controlled at what level?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Time Cards > Actual Effort Update: The property to update actual effort from time cards is controlled at the Project Level (C). Per p1603, the 'Allow time card reporting on' field on the project form determines the level at which time cards are created and actual effort is tracked — this is a per-project setting, not global, program, or portfolio level.

questions.stem: What is a resource event?

options.text: An event scheduled by a project manager.
A block of time that a resource spends on a task.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Resource Events > Definition: A resource event is a block of time that a resource spends on a task (C). Resource events are calendar entries generated by resource allocations, representing scheduled work time for a specific task. They are system-generated (not manually scheduled by PMs), are not external events (A), and are scheduled activities (not non-scheduled as in D).

questions.stem: What happens to resource allocations with actual hours after a resource plan is cancelled?

options.text: The allocated hours remain until the project is closed.
The allocated hours become zero and the actual hours are retained.
A resource plan with actual hours cannot be canceled.
They are automatically moved to the next resource plan in the project.

questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Resource Plans > Cancellation with Actual Hours: When a resource plan is cancelled, allocated hours become zero and actual hours are retained (B). Per p1416: 'If there are any actual hours logged against an allocation, that allocation isn't deleted. But the allocated hours become zero and the actual hours are retained.' The plan can be cancelled even with actual hours (C is false).

questions.stem: A program is a container for the following except for:
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Programs > Container Contents: A program is NOT a container for portfolios (D). Programs contain program tasks (A), issues (B), and cost plans (C). The relationship is inverted — a program can be PART OF a portfolio (p1537: 'A program can be part of a portfolio'), but programs do not contain portfolios. Portfolios are higher-level containers that hold programs.

questions.stem: Which related lists should primarily be used to capture financial data in a project? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Projects > Financial Related Lists: The two related lists primarily used for financial data in a project are Cost Plans (A) and Monetary Benefit Plans (D). Cost Plans capture planned and actual costs by fiscal period. Monetary Benefit Plans capture expected financial returns. Risks (B) track project risks. Programs (C) show organizational structure, not financial data.

questions.stem: Use this table to configure the parameters displayed on a project card on the My Projects Space page of the Project Workspace.
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Project Workspace > Card Configuration Table: The pm_home_page_config table (D) is used to configure the parameters on project cards in My Projects Space. Per p1344: 'Set the display columns for row 2 of the card in PM Home Page Configuration [pm_home_page_config] table.' pm_project (C) stores project data. pm_toplevel_project (A) and project_template_config (B) are unrelated.

questions.stem: Which statement defines the Project Workspace?

options.text: A central location to view of all projects in a portfolio to prioritize work
A central location for creating and managing projects
A central location for viewing and assessing business demands
A central location transform the navigation of lists and forms into an interactive graphical experience

questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Project Workspace > Definition: Project Workspace is a central location for creating and managing projects (B). It provides project managers with tools to plan tasks, manage financials, track resources, and monitor project progress. Viewing portfolio projects (A) is the Portfolio Workbench. Assessing demands (C) is the Demand Workbench.

questions.stem: A user’s availability is calculated as:

options.text: Allocated hours divided by the total capacity
Sum of allocated and confirmed hours, divided by the total capacity

questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Resource Management > Availability: User availability is calculated as capacity minus allocation (B). Availability = total work capacity − allocated hours. This is the standard formula for determining how much work time a resource has remaining. Allocated time alone (A) is not availability. Dividing by capacity (C, D) gives utilization percentage, not availability.

questions.stem: A project expense line is cost associated with a specific source, except for:
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Expense Lines > Invalid Source: Program (D) is NOT a valid expense line source. Expense lines are costs associated with specific sources such as a resource/user (A), fixed assets (B), or software/CIs (C). Programs are organizational containers for projects and demands — they are not direct cost sources for individual expense lines.

questions.stem: Which of the following can be used to calculate planned cost when creating a resource plan? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Resource Plans > Planned Cost Calculation: Two sources used to calculate planned cost when creating a resource plan are: Default rate (A) — the fallback hourly rate used when no other rate is specified — and Rate card (B) — the labor rate card which provides date-effective hourly rates. Per p1461, planned cost = planned hours × hourly rate, derived from rate override, labor rate card, or default rate. Demand rate (C) and project rate (D) are not standard terms.

questions.stem: If a project manager is responsible for approving time sheets or submitting time cards on behalf of team members, they should be given what role?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Time Cards > Approval Role: If a project manager needs to approve time sheets or submit time cards on behalf of team members, they should have the timecard_admin role (C). Per p1560, the time card admin can approve/reject time cards and create or edit time cards of any user when they are in Pending or Rejected state. form_admin (A), approval_admin (B), and activity_admin (D) are not applicable.

questions.stem: Which property controls the changes in cost and resource plans with respect to the change in the start date of a demand or project?

options.text: ‘Change Resource Plan, Cost Plan and Benefit Plan Start Date with Demand or Project Start Date Change’.
‘Enable altering of planned date for task in WIP/Closed’.
‘Calculate ROI percentage based on a project’s estimated cost and its net value’.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Properties > Start Date Change: The property 'Change Resource Plan, Cost Plan and Benefit Plan Start Date with Demand or Project Start Date Change' (A) controls whether related plans are automatically shifted when a demand or project start date changes. Options B, C, and D control different behaviors: WIP date editing, task rollup, and ROI calculation respectively.

questions.stem: If the ‘Move project for WIP projects’ property is enabled, project tasks associated with the project are also moved, except for tasks in which of the following states? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Move Project > Excluded Task States: When 'Move project for WIP projects' is enabled, tasks in Closed (B) and Work in Progress (C) states are NOT moved when the project start date changes. Tasks in other states (Pending/Open) are moved. Closed tasks have already been completed and WIP tasks are actively in progress — neither should be rescheduled automatically.

questions.stem: Expenses and costs for a particular demand should be estimated before screening. When preparing the financials of a demand, what determines the present value of future cash flows?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Demand Financials > Present Value: The Discount Rate % (D) determines the present value of future cash flows on a demand. Per p1020, 'at a 12% discount rate, $1.00 today is worth $0.80 in two years' — the discount rate is the annual interest rate applied in the NPV calculation. Financial Return (A) is an input value. Planned ROI (B) is derived. IRR (C) is the rate that makes NPV zero.

questions.stem: Idea [im_idea_core] is directly extended from which table?

options.text: It is not extended from any table.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Ideation > Table Hierarchy: The Idea [im_idea_core] table is directly extended from the Task table (D). Like many ServiceNow work items, the Idea table extends Task to inherit fields like number, assignment, state, and description. Project (A) is a sibling task-extended table. Idea Modules (C) are configuration records, not the base table.

questions.stem: The Defect and Enhancement type choices on a demand form are available only when which plugin is installed?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Demands > Defect and Enhancement Types: The Defect and Enhancement type choices on a demand form are available only when the Agile Development 2.0 plugin is installed (A). Per p1013, Enhancement appears as a Strategic demand type and Defect appears as an Operational type — both require Agile Development 2.0. Ideation (B), Test Management (C), and Investment Funding (D) do not activate these types.

questions.stem: The color band at the top of the project card in Project Workspace displays what project attribute?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Project Cards > Color Band: The color band at the top of a project card in Project Workspace displays the project Status (C). The color band shows the RAG (Red/Amber/Green) status indicator, providing a quick visual health indicator. Issues (A) and Risk (B) are separate tracked items. State (D) is the lifecycle state (Draft/In Progress/Closed), not the RAG status color.

questions.stem: Which demand category would a demand manager select, if they need to create an enhancement?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Demand Categories > Enhancement: A demand manager selects the Strategic category (B) to create an enhancement. Per p1013, Enhancement is a Type available when the Category is Strategic: 'The following demand types are available if the demand category is Strategic: Continual Improvement Management, Enhancement, Project, Epic, Story...' Change and Defect are Operational types. Operational (D) is for changes/defects.

questions.stem: On the demand form, what does the Discount Rate impact?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Demand Financials > Discount Rate: The Discount Rate % impacts Net Present Value (NPV) (D) on the demand form. Per p1020, NPV is the 'present value of future cash based on the given annual interest rate' — the discount rate is this annual rate used in the NPV formula. IRR (A) is independently calculated as the rate making NPV=0. ROI (B) uses planned return/cost. Financial Benefit (C) is an input value.

questions.stem: As a demand manager, you can view an artifact from a demand. What artifacts are part of a demand?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Demand Artifacts > Viewable Artifacts: Artifacts a demand manager can view from a demand include Project, Defect, and Change Requests (C). Per p986, when a demand is accepted, the resulting artifacts are Project, Enhancement, Change, or Defect. Option C (Project, Defect, Requests) maps to Project, Defect, and Change Requests — the best fit among options. Decision/Risk (B) are RIDAC elements within a demand, not output artifacts. Incidents/Problems (A) are not demand artifacts.

questions.stem: As an it_pps_admin, what can you use to detect corrupt data in a project, such as tasks with invalid parents or cyclic relations in a project?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Project Diagnostics > Corrupt Data: Project Diagnostics (A) is used to detect corrupt data in a project, such as tasks with invalid parents or cyclic relations. Per p1146: 'Use Project Diagnostics to detect corrupt project data... using the Application Diagnostics Tool to detect corrupt data in a project, such as tasks with invalid parents, tasks without top tasks, and invalid or cyclic relations.' Role required: it_pps_admin. Other diagnostics (B, C, D) are unrelated tools.

questions.stem: In which scenario would using the Copy Project action NOT result in a new project record being created?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Copy Project > Non-creation Scenario: The Copy Project action does NOT result in a new project record when copying partial projects (D). Copy Partial Projects copies selected tasks from source into an existing target project — it does not create a new project record. Copy Project (A), Copy New Project (B), and Copy Sub-projects (C) all generate new project records. Partial project copy is additive to an existing project.

questions.stem: When copying a source project to a target project, what fields are copied by default? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Copy Project > Default Fields: Per p1064: 'By default only the short description, planned dates and duration fields are copied from source project to the target project.' Therefore: Duration fields (B), Short description (C), and Planned dates (D) are copied. Number (A) is auto-generated. State (E) is not copied — it resets to new. Additional fields require the copy.additional_attributes property.

questions.stem: The Project management application supports two types of external dependencies. What are they? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > External Dependencies > Types: The Project Management application supports two types of external dependencies: Hard (A) and Soft (C). Per p1054: 'The Project management application supports two types of external dependencies - hard and soft.' Hard dependencies auto-propagate changes; soft dependencies trigger notifications only. Milestone (B), Task (D), and Change (E) dependencies are not the two external dependency types.

questions.stem: In order to map custom fields from Microsoft Project to ServiceNow when importing a project, you must first:

options.text: Export the project to XML format
Create custom fields in your ServiceNow instance

questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > MS Project Import > Custom Field Mapping: To map custom fields from Microsoft Project to ServiceNow, you must first create custom fields in your ServiceNow instance (D). Custom fields must exist in ServiceNow before they can be mapped during the import process. Configuring the Project form (A) or exporting to XML (B) come after. Importing the project (C) happens after field mapping is configured.

questions.stem: What is the formula for Committed Utilization?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Resource Utilization > Committed Utilization: The formula for Committed Utilization is Allocated Hours / Capacity (A). Committed utilization measures hard-allocated (confirmed and allocated) hours against total capacity. Option B includes both Allocated and Confirmed, which would be total utilization. Option C is Confirmed-only utilization. Option D uses assigned hours, which is a different metric.

questions.stem: How many days is the default sprint length if the length cannot be calculated from the sprint?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Agile > Default Sprint Length: The default sprint length is 14 days (B) when the length cannot be calculated from the sprint. Per p2064, the property com.snc.sdlc.scrum.pp.default_sprint_length controls this, and p557 confirms the standard 14-day sprint length. Options 12, 16, and 18 are not the ServiceNow default sprint duration.

questions.stem: Risks and issues submitted in which forms will be included in the Program record? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Programs > Risks and Issues Inclusion: Risks and issues submitted in project (A), demand (C), and program (D) forms are included in the Program record. Per p1537, programs track risks and issues from their associated projects and demands, plus program-level risks/issues. Ideas (B) are pre-demand artifacts. Portfolio (E) is a higher-level container — its risks are not rolled into programs.

questions.stem: The Program Management application provides the following capabilities to the program manager (Choose three.)

options.text: Create tasks specific to the program.
Create a program by adding related projects and demands
Manage ideas specific to the program

questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Program Management > Capabilities: Three Program Management capabilities for program managers: Create program-specific tasks (A), track program costs (B), and create a program by adding related projects and demands (C). Per p1536-1538, program management groups related projects/demands and tracks costs/schedules. Creating releases for sprints (D) is Agile Release scope. Managing program-specific ideas (E) is Innovation Management scope.

questions.stem: Which feature provides a central location for portfolio managers to create and track the roadmap for project and demand execution?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Portfolio Workbench > Central Location: The Portfolio Workbench (B) provides a central location for portfolio managers to view and monitor progress of programs, projects, and demands in the portfolio. Per p1481: 'The portfolio workbench provides a central location to view and monitor the progress of the program, the projects, and demands that are part of the portfolio.' Program Workbench (A) is program-level. Demand Workbench (D) is demand-specific.

questions.stem: Why is it recommended to keep the value of the property 'com.snc.project.task.max_task_duration' to 2600 or under?

options.text: Best practices states projects should be no longer than 5 years.
The system is unable to handle more than 2600 tasks.
Because projects longer than 2600 days will no longer load.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Project Properties > Max Task Duration: The property com.snc.project.task.max_task_duration is recommended at 2600 or under to avoid application memory issues (C). Projects with excessively long task durations consume disproportionate memory when loading the Planning Console and calculating schedules. Large values can cause out-of-memory errors. The limit is not about 5-year best practices (A) or an inability to handle tasks (B) or load projects (D).

questions.stem: Which role can create a project status report in the Project Workspace?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Project Workspace > Status Report Role: The it_project_manager role (C) is required to create a project status report in the Project Workspace. Per p1095: the Status Report tab is accessed in Project Workspace, and per p1278: 'the it_project_manager role is required to create a document template... in the Project Workspace.' itil (A) and it_demand_manager (B) have no project workspace creation rights. it_project_user (D) is read-only.

questions.stem: When creating a program, which of the following cannot be part of multiple programs? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Programs > Multiple Program Restriction: A project (B) and a demand (C) cannot be part of multiple programs. Per p1537: 'A project or demand cannot be part of multiple programs.' Tasks (A) can be created in multiple contexts. A portfolio (D) can contain multiple programs but is not restricted from being associated with multiple entities — and programs cannot be part of multiple portfolios (not programs).

questions.stem: Winch role allows you to allocate a resource?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Resource Management > Allocation Role: The resource_manager role (D) is required to allocate a resource. Resource managers own the allocation process — they confirm and allocate resource plans, manage group capacity, and approve resource requests. resource_user (A) can view but not allocate. it_project_user (B) is a project viewer. business_stakeholder (C) is not a standard PPM role.

questions.stem: Why would a program manager create a program? (Choose two.)

options.text: To define the number of sprints

questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Programs > Purpose: A program manager creates a program to manage related demands (A) and related projects (C). Per p1536: 'A program helps you to logically group related projects or demands under a single entity.' Defining sprint counts (B) is a Scrum/Agile task. Managing portfolios (D) is the portfolio manager's role, not program manager's.

questions.stem: Which role in Protect Portfolio Management contains both the resource_user and it_demand manager roles?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Role Hierarchy > it_project_manager: The it_project_manager role (A) contains both resource_user and it_demand_manager. Per p1816, it_project_manager includes resource_user among its contained roles, and the PPM role hierarchy also grants it_demand_manager. scrum_master (B) is Agile-focused. itil (C) is ITSM. timeline_admin (D) is not a PPM role containing both.

questions.stem: In order to allocate an operational resource plan from the Resource Allocation Workbench, which property must be enabled?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Resource Allocation Workbench > Operational Plans: To allocate an operational resource plan from the Resource Allocation Workbench, enable property com.snc.resource_management.create_and_manage_operational_resource_plans_from_raw (B). This property specifically enables the operational resource plan management capability within the RAW interface. The other properties control project move behavior (A), percentage allocation thresholds (C), and soft allocation calendar visibility (D).

questions.stem: The basics of Demand Management include (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Demand Management > Basics: Two basics of Demand Management are: Identify stakeholders (A) and Create assessment categories (B). Stakeholder identification enables assessment routing, and assessment categories define scoring criteria. Evaluating and qualifying tasks (C) is project task management. Creating ideas (D) precedes demand creation — it is Innovation Management, not Demand Management basics.

questions.stem: At which point in the Demand Management lifecycle do assessments get sent to stakeholders?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Demand Management > Assessment Timing: Assessments are sent to stakeholders during the Screening state (A). Per p961: 'The demand manager can screen the demand and send surveys to stakeholders to complete assessments.' Screening is when the demand manager evaluates feasibility and gathers stakeholder input via assessments. Creation (B) and Draft (initial) states precede screening. Planning (C) comes after approval.

questions.stem: When working with demands, which field must be set to “Yes” in order for a user to receive an assessment?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Demands > Assessment Recipient: The Assessment recipient field must be set to 'Yes' on a stakeholder record for that user to receive an assessment survey (B). This field controls whether a stakeholder receives assessment notifications. Approver (A) is for approval workflow. Influence (C) and Level of Interest (D) are stakeholder characterization fields.

questions.stem: Where is the normalization process used?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Demand Assessment > Normalization: The normalization process is used in assessment scoring (B). When scoring multiple demands on assessment metrics, normalization ensures scores are comparable across demands regardless of absolute values. This process is part of demand assessment evaluation, not approval (A), risk records (C), or cost plan updates (D).

questions.stem: The selections from the Category and Type fields determine the artifact that can be created from a demand. The artifacts can be (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Demands > Artifacts: Three artifacts that can be created from a demand via Category/Type are: enhancement (A), defect (B), and change (C). Per p1013, Strategic category enables Enhancement and Operational category enables Defect and Change artifacts. Resource (D) is not a demand conversion artifact. Task (E) is too generic and not a specific demand type.

questions.stem: In the default system, when working with demands, what two assessment metrics are supported when taking an assessment survey? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Demand Assessment > Default Metrics: Two default assessment metric categories supported via survey are Strategic Alignment (A) and Risk (B). Per p959, the default assessment metric categories for demand include Strategic Alignment and Risk Rating (survey-based). Size (C) uses the T-shirt size field directly from the form. Cost (D) is not a default assessment survey metric.

questions.stem: The colors and quadrant labels used in the central location for viewing and assessing business demands?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Demand Workbench > Configuration: Colors and quadrant labels for the demand workbench (the central demand assessment location) are configured in the Workbench Config - Demand record (A). This configuration record controls the bubble chart appearance including colors, quadrant labels, and axis definitions. Demand Roadmap (B), Demand-Config (C), and System Properties (D) are not the configuration location.

questions.stem: Under the Preferences tab on the Demand form, you have the option to (Choose two.)

options.text: Close a demand on closure of a project
Close a demand on creation of a project

questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Demand Form > Preferences Tab: Two options on the Demand form Preferences tab are: Close a demand on closure of a project (B) and Close a demand on creation of a project (C). Per p1022, the 'Close Demand' preference controls automatic demand closure timing. Adding financial benefit (A) is in cost/benefit plans. Adding risk score (D) is in Assessment Data section.

questions.stem: When a demand is converted to a project, the following fields retain the start and due date (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Demand to Project > Date Fields: When a demand is converted to a project, the Approved start date (A) and Approved end date (C) are retained. These formal approved dates carry over to the project. Actual start date (B) and Actual end date (D) are not retained during conversion as they track real execution timing, which resets when the project begins.

questions.stem: Which roles can add stakeholders to a Portfolio? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Portfolios > Stakeholder Roles: Two roles that can add stakeholders to a portfolio are it_demand_manager (B) and it_pps_admin (C). The PPS Admin has full administrative access. The demand manager manages demand aspects including stakeholder associations at the portfolio level. it_project_user (A) has view-only access. it_demand_user (D) is a basic viewer role.

questions.stem: When Agile Development 2.0 and Test Management 2.0 plugins are activated, the project manager can create and edit which of the following phase types depending on execution type? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Projects > Phase Types: With Agile Development 2.0 and Test Management 2.0 activated, project managers can create Test phases (A) and Agile phases (B). Per p903, the Agile phase option appears only when PPM and Agile 2.0 are installed, and Test phase appears only when PPM and Test Management 2.0 are installed. List (C) and VTB (D) are not project phase types.

questions.stem: The combination of the user and the assigned portfolio must be unique when adding a user to which registry?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Stakeholder Registry > Uniqueness: The combination of user and assigned portfolio must be unique when adding a user to the Stakeholder Registry (D). The Stakeholder Register Form enforces that each user-portfolio combination is unique. UX Page Registry (A), Event Registry (B), and Application Registry (C) are platform registries unrelated to PPM stakeholders.

questions.stem: How can the planned start date on a WIP/Closed task be changed?

options.text: By setting the property – 'Enable firing of Business Rules on save from Planning Console'
By setting the property – 'Enable alter of planned date with Actual for Manual Project'
By setting the property – 'Enable altering of planned date(s) for task in WIP/Closed'
By setting the property – 'Enable project cost rollup'

questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Project Properties > WIP/Closed Task Dates: The planned start date on a WIP/Closed task can be changed by setting the property 'Enable altering of planned date(s) for task in WIP/Closed' (C). This specific property unlocks date editing for tasks in these otherwise locked states. Options A, B, and D control different behaviors: planning console BRs, manual project dates, and cost rollup respectively.

questions.stem: Project score is calculated based on the individual scores of the following attributes (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Project Scoring > Attributes: Project score is calculated based on Risk Score (B) and Value Score (D). Per p1021, the demand/project score is calculated from individual Risk and Value scores. Alignment Score (A) and Strategy Score (C) are not the standard scoring components in the base PPM scoring framework.

questions.stem: The Project Management application enables users to create parent-child relationships between tasks and dependencies, such as finish-to-start and finish-to-finish, between tasks. How many relationships can exist between two tasks?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Task Relationships > Count: Up to four relationships can exist between two tasks (D). The four dependency types are: Finish-to-Start, Start-to-Start, Finish-to-Finish, and Start-to-Finish (p1042). Each represents a distinct type of predecessor-successor relationship, allowing all four to potentially exist between the same two tasks simultaneously.

questions.stem: Which of the following defines a parent-child relationship? (Choose two.)

options.text: Parent-child task relationships do not have any effect on task time constraints
A parent-child relationship is not saved as a record in any table
A parent-child task must finish before another begins
Any number of child tasks can be nested under a parent task with or without any dependencies

questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Parent-Child Tasks > Characteristics: Two true statements about parent-child relationships are: a parent-child relationship is not saved as a record in any table (B) — unlike dependencies which use task_rel_task, parent-child hierarchy is tracked via parent field on task records — and any number of child tasks can be nested under a parent with or without dependencies (D). Per p1041, 'no restrictions on creating child tasks.'

questions.stem: What can a time card admin or a project manager create to define specific activities in a project?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Time Cards > Specific Activities: A time card admin or project manager can create Subcategories (C) to define specific activities in a project. Subcategories provide granular activity definitions within time card categories, enabling more detailed time tracking. Policies (A) define time sheet rules. Time Sheets (B) capture logged time. Time Cards (D) record actual time spent.

questions.stem: Who can access a project when it is imported into a teamspace from Microsoft Project into ServiceNow?

options.text: A project cannot be imported into a teamspace
Only users who can access the teamspace

questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Teamspaces > Import Access: When a project is imported into a teamspace from Microsoft Project, only users who can access the teamspace can access the project (C). Teamspace projects are restricted to users with the appropriate teamspace-specific roles. All users (D) cannot access teamspace projects. The import is supported (B is false).

questions.stem: The overall health of a program rolls up from the latest status report of each project in the program. The status is indicated by which colors? (Choose three.)
