questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Programs > Status Colors: The program health rollup uses three colors: Yellow (B), Green (C), and Red (D). Per p1546: 'The status is indicated using red, green, and yellow colors by default.' These represent the standard RAG (Red/Amber/Green) traffic light health indicators. Orange (A) is not one of the standard PPM status colors.

questions.stem: The PPM Strategic Spend Trading-Generate Strategy/Goal Allocation Breakdowns for Projects and Demands scheduled job is installed, when which of the following is activated?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Strategic Spend Tracking > Scheduled Job: The scheduled job for generating strategy/goal allocation breakdowns is installed when Strategic Spend Tracking for PPM (C) is activated. Per p1784-1785, the Strategic Spend Tracking plugin includes this scheduled job as a component. PPM Standard (B), Predictive Intelligence (A), and Scenario Planning (D) do not install this specific job.

questions.stem: Each teamspace has its own (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Teamspaces > Own Tables: Each teamspace has its own Project table (A) and Demand table (C). Per p1137, teamspace 1 has Teamspace_1 Project [tsp1_project] and each teamspace has its own prefixed project and demand tables. Resource (B) is shared across teamspaces. Problem (D) is an ITSM table not part of teamspace architecture.

questions.stem: During the allocation process, when named resources are allocated to a plan, where is resource cost derived from?

options.text: Labor rate card for the user
Labor rate card for the fiscal period
Cost specified on the resource allocation

questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Resource Plans > Allocation Cost Source: During the allocation process, resource cost for named resources is derived from the labor rate card for the user (A). Per p1469, the hourly rate source hierarchy is: Rate model (if populated) → Labor rate card → default system property. The labor rate card is the primary cost source when no rate model is specified. Costs are not stored directly on the allocation (C) or user record (D).

questions.stem: What is the formula for Forecasted Utilization?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Resource Utilization > Forecasted Utilization: The formula for Forecasted Utilization is (Allocated Hours + Confirmed Hours) / Capacity (B). Forecasted utilization combines both hard allocations (Allocated) and soft allocations (Confirmed) against total capacity. This differs from Committed Utilization (Allocated Hours / Capacity) which counts only hard bookings. Confirmed Hours alone (C) is partial utilization. Assigned Hours (D) is a different metric.

questions.stem: What are the allocation types available on a resource plan? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Resource Plans > Allocation Types: Three allocation types available on a resource plan are Weekly (A), Monthly (C), and Plan Duration (D). Per p1468: 'Monthly: 3 allocation records... Weekly: 14 allocation records... Plan Duration: Only 1 record for the entire duration of the resource plan.' Yearly (B) and Daily (E) are not standard allocation type options on a ServiceNow resource plan.

questions.stem: Resource plan costs are divided into (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Resource Plans > Cost Categories: Resource plan costs are divided into Planned Cost (A), Allocated Cost (C), and Actual Cost (E). Planned cost reflects the cost during Planning/Requested states; Allocated cost is calculated once the plan is in Allocated state; Actual cost comes from approved time cards. Forecast Cost (B) and Expense Cost (D) are not the three standard resource plan cost categories.

questions.stem: On a resource plan, when the attribute for "Derive assignee list from resource plan" is set to true, in what state must the plan be to allow a resource to be added to the assignee field?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Resource Plans > Derive Assignee: When 'Derive assignee list from resource plan' is true, the resource plan must be in the Allocated state (C) to allow a resource to be added to the assignee field. Only Allocated plans have hard allocations binding specific users, making those users available as assignees. Confirmed (A) is a soft allocation without specific user commitment. Requested (B) and Planning (D) states are prior to allocation.

questions.stem: When a user's schedule changes, what action needs to be taken to update their existing data?

options.text: Update calendar manually to reflect the changed capacity

questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Resource Capacity > Schedule Change Update: When a user's schedule changes, the 'Update Resource Capacity' action (D) must be taken to update their existing capacity data. Per p1436: 'Use the Update resource capacity related link' to update a user's capacity based on their schedule. This populates capacity in all resource aggregate tables. No action (A) leaves stale data. Manual calendar updates (C) and project plan updates (B) don't update resource capacity tables.

questions.stem: If a resource plan is not associated manually to a time card, then a resource plan is auto-associated. The auto-association is done based on which of the following in the time card?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Time Cards > Resource Plan Auto-Association: Auto-association of a resource plan to a time card is based on the selected task (A) in the time card. Per p1422: 'If a resource plan isn't associated manually to a time card, then a resource plan is auto-associated. The auto-association is done based on the selected Task in the time card.' Hard allocation (B) is a prerequisite for associating, but the auto-association key is the task. Soft allocation (C) and resource type (D) are not used.

questions.stem: Actuals on a resource plan are updated by what activity?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Resource Plans > Actuals Update Trigger: Actuals on a resource plan are updated when a time card is approved (D). The approval and processing of time cards triggers the update of actual hours on the associated resource plan. User submission alone (A) is not sufficient. Project manager entry (B) is not the mechanism. Resource plan approval (C) does not update actuals — time card approval does.

questions.stem: What must a resource plan contain if a resource plan is associated with a time card?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Time Cards > Resource Plan Requirement: A resource plan associated with a time card must contain hard allocation bookings (C). Per p1422: 'A resource plan can be associated with a time card only if the resource plan contains hard allocations for the user.' Soft allocation bookings (A) are insufficient for time card association. Allocation spread type (B, D) is a separate configuration unrelated to the time card association requirement.

questions.stem: What are the offset types in Benefit Plans?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Benefit Plans > Offset Types: The offset types in Benefit Plans are Start Date and End Date (B). Per p1199 and p2107, the Offset type field options include None, Milestone, Start Date, and End Date — Start Date and End Date being the two date-based offset types. Rate Card (A), Risk (C), and Cost (D) are not Benefit Plan offset type options. The offset type determines when the benefit plan begins relative to the project dates.

questions.stem: Which field, referenced from the cost plan, determines if a cost plan is Capex or Opex?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Cost Plans > CAPEX/OPEX Field: The Cost type field (resource_type) (C) referenced from the cost plan determines if a cost plan is CAPEX or OPEX. Per p1251: 'cost_type - view financials by cost types such as Hardware Opex, External labor Capex, Software Capex, Software Opex.' The cost type classifies labor and non-labor costs as capital or operational. Resource category (A), currency type (B), and resource plan reference (D) do not determine CAPEX/OPEX classification.

questions.stem: You can forecast future costs of projects based on (Choose two.)

options.text: Changes in project such as project requirements

questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Budget Forecasting > Forecast Basis: Future costs of projects can be forecasted based on actual cost incurred (A) and changes in project requirements (B). Per p1507: 'forecast the future costs of projects and portfolios based on the actual cost and changed project requirements.' Incident cost (C) and paired instances (D) are not inputs to project cost forecasting.

questions.stem: To integrate Investment Funding with PPM, what plugin must be activated?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Investment Funding > Plugin: To integrate Investment Funding with PPM, the Investment Funding for PPM plugin (A) — com.snc.investment_planning_pmo — must be activated. Per p1516: 'Verify that the Investment Funding for PPM (com.snc.investment_planning_pmo) plugin is activated. This plugin needs to be activated only when you want to retrieve the target amount for a portfolio.' The base Investment Funding (B) and Financial Planning (C) plugins are separate from the PPM-specific variant.

questions.stem: A customer needs to know what activity type is associated to time entries in the project so that they can capitalize build tasks. What is the best method to do this?

options.text: Leverage project time categories to classify the time.
Create a capital protect task flag.
Put all capital project tasks in one phase and report from those tasks.

questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Time Categories > Capitalizing Build Tasks: The best method to associate activity types with time entries for capitalizing build tasks is to leverage project time categories (A). Time categories classify the nature of work logged on time cards, enabling cost accounting systems to identify which hours are capitalizable. Creating task flags (B) or grouping tasks in a phase (C) are indirect workarounds. Creating an incident (D) is unrelated.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the default schedule for the Project Management application?

options.text: Repeats every week on weekdays Monday through Friday from 8:00am to noon and 1:00-5:00pm
Repeats every week on weekdays Monday through Friday
Repeats every week on weekdays Monday through Friday. Includes the child schedule U.S. Holidays
Repeats every week on weekdays Monday through Friday from 9:00am to 5:00pm

questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Schedules > Default Schedule: The default schedule for the Project Management application repeats every week on weekdays Monday through Friday from 8:00am to noon and 1:00pm to 5:00pm (A). This standard 8-hour workday with a 1-hour lunch break is the OOB default schedule. Option B omits the time specification. Option C adds the U.S. Holidays child schedule. Option D uses 9am-5pm which differs from the default.

questions.stem: Demand managers can enhance a demand request by adding the following: (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Demand Management > Enhancements: Three items demand managers can add to enhance a demand request are Requirements (A), Tasks (B), and Stakeholders (E). Per p988: 'Demand managers can create as many requirements as needed' and 'When adding a stakeholder from the demand form...' Demand tasks (B) allow tracking demand-specific work. Expense lines (C) are financial records handled separately. Decisions (D) are RIDAC elements, not standard demand enhancement items.

questions.stem: To provide more meaningful information to senior management, you can view the FTE value under which of the following reports?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Resource Reports > FTE View: FTE values can be viewed under Allocation Details (C) reports. Per p1444: 'Allocation details - A tabular breakdown of all allocation requests (soft bookings), committed allocations (hard bookings), availability, capacity, and actual hours.' Allocation Details provides a view rich enough to include FTE context for senior management. Resource Aggregate Reports (A) focus on capacity. Committed Utilization (D) is a ratio metric without FTE detail.

questions.stem: Which option should be used if you want to select the resource rate on the resource plan?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Resource Plans > Rate Selection: Rate override (A) is used when selecting the resource rate directly on the resource plan. Per p1473: 'The hourly rate is derived from: Resource rate from the resource plan, if the Rate Override option is selected.' Rate override lets the PM specify a custom rate at the resource plan level. Labor rate card (B) is a fallback in the rate hierarchy. Rate model (C) is a structured rate configuration. Planned cost (D) is a calculated output, not a rate selector.

questions.stem: Which of the following tasks can be performed when innovation Management is integrated with Universal Request? (Choose two.)

options.text: Transfer an idea to another department
Create a project from a universal request
Send a universal request to a demand manager for review
Create an idea from a universal request

questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Innovation Management > Universal Request Integration: Two tasks when Innovation Management is integrated with Universal Request are: Transfer an idea to another department (A) and Create an idea from a universal request (D). Per p913 and p929-p930, the integration enables creating ideas from Universal Request tickets and transferring ideas between departments. Creating a project from UR (B) and sending UR to demand manager (C) are not specific capabilities of this integration.

questions.stem: The RIDAC workflow can be modified by using which recommended feature?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > RIDAC > Workflow Modification: The RIDAC workflow is best modified using Flow Designer (C). Flow Designer is the recommended modern tool in ServiceNow for modifying and extending workflows, including RIDAC processes. Workflow Editor (D) is the legacy tool and not recommended for new modifications. Service Catalog (A) and Project Form (B) are unrelated to RIDAC workflow modification.

questions.stem: A project status report can be viewed from which of the following areas? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Project Status Report > Viewing Locations: A project status report can be viewed from four areas: Project workspace (B), Project status form (C), Project record (E), and Portfolio workbench (F). Per p1096: viewing options include Project workspace, Project record, and Project Status form. The Portfolio workbench also surfaces project status reports. Program record (A) does not display project status reports. Planning console (D) is for task scheduling.

questions.stem: Which role is required to define custom schedules?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Schedules > Admin Role: The system admin (C) role is required to define custom schedules. Custom work schedules are system-level configurations that control when resources are available and how project task durations are calculated. resource_manager (A) manages resource allocation, pps_resource (B) is a basic resource role, and resource_user (D) has even less access.

questions.stem: As an administrator, what can you use to customize the PPM Mobile application?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Mobile > Customization Tool: As an administrator, Mobile Studio (A) is used to customize the PPM Mobile application. Mobile Studio is ServiceNow's tool for building and customizing mobile app experiences. Now Platform App Engine (B) is for building applications generally. Now Mobile App (C) is the end-user app. Service Catalog (D) is for request management.

questions.stem: What are the three default project template configuration records available in the Template Config module? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Templates > Default Config Records: Three default project template configuration records in the Template Config module are: Project subtask (A), Project task (B), and Project (D). Per p1115, the default template configuration includes the project root (pm_project = Project), project tasks, and project subtasks as the standard template hierarchy. Portfolio task (C), Program task (E), and Task (F) are not included.

questions.stem: If a sub-project and parent project have different project currencies, this property should be set to true for cost roll-ups.
questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Multicurrency > Cost Rollup Property: The property com.snc.project.multicurrency.rollup_if_different (A) should be set to true for cost roll-ups when a sub-project and parent project have different project currencies. Per p1237, this property controls whether costs roll up across projects with mismatched currencies. The other properties (B, C, D) control start date rollup, attribute copying, and ROI calculation respectively.

questions.stem: Can an it_project_manager convert a task to a milestone?

options.text: Yes, if the task is assigned to the project manager.
Yes, by right-clicking on the task in the Planning Console.
No, the PPS admin role is also required.
No, this can only be done by a system admin.

questions.explanation: [Zurich] PPM > Planning Console > Task to Milestone: Yes, an it_project_manager can convert a task to a milestone by right-clicking on the task in the Planning Console (B). Per p1086: 'You can also convert a task to milestone through Planning console tasks.' The conversion sets Duration to 0 making it a diamond milestone. PPS Admin (C) or system admin (D) roles are not required for this action.

questions.stem: Transition, Mobilize, Prepare and Conduct are included in which stage of the Now Create methodology?
questions.explanation: [Platform] PPM > Now Create > Methodology Stages: Transition, Mobilize, Prepare, and Conduct are phases included in the Prepare stage (D) of the Now Create methodology. The Now Create project delivery methodology organizes these four phases under the Prepare stage, which covers readiness activities before implementation begins. Initiate (C) is an earlier stage and Close (B) is the final stage.
